scenes.title: Multi Row Subqueries
scenes.narration: A multi row subquery returns more than one row, so the outer query must use an operator that can handle a whole set of values.

scenes.title: Operators that accept many rows
bullets: IN matches the outer value against any value in the set.
ANY compares against the set using a relational operator, succeeding if any match.
ALL compares against the set, succeeding only if every value matches.
scenes.narration: The IN operator checks whether the outer value equals any value produced by the subquery. ANY pairs with an operator like greater-than and succeeds if the comparison holds for at least one value in the set. ALL uses the same relational operators but requires the comparison to hold against every value returned.

scenes.title: Employees in European departments
scenes.code:
SELECT employee_id, first_name, dept_id
FROM employees
WHERE dept_id IN (
    SELECT id
    FROM departments
    WHERE region = 'EU'
);
scenes.narration: The inner query builds a list of department ids where the region is Europe. Because that list can contain many rows, we use IN rather than an equals sign. The outer query then returns every employee whose department id appears anywhere in that list.

scenes.title: ANY versus ALL

left.title: > ANY (set)
points: True if greater than at least one value

right.title: > ALL (set)
points: True only if greater than every value

scenes.narration: With greater-than ANY, a row qualifies if it beats even the smallest value in the set, so it behaves like a comparison against the minimum. With greater-than ALL, a row qualifies only if it beats every value, which is the same as comparing against the maximum. Choosing between them comes down to whether you need a loose or a strict threshold.

scenes.title: Salaries higher than every intern
scenes.code:
SELECT first_name, salary
FROM employees
WHERE salary > ALL (
    SELECT salary
    FROM employees
    WHERE job_title = 'Intern'
);
scenes.narration: The subquery returns the salary of each intern as a set of values. Using greater-than ALL, an employee qualifies only when their salary exceeds every intern salary. In practice this filters down to people paid more than the highest paid intern.

scenes.text: Reach for IN, ANY, or ALL whenever a subquery can return several rows. Using a plain equals sign against a multi row set will raise an error.
scenes.narration: Whenever your subquery might return several rows, choose IN, ANY, or ALL to handle the set correctly. A plain equals sign expects one value and will fail against a multi row result.
